roles_and_gates.parent: Owns Gate 3, integration, shared contract confirmation, scope completeness, accepted findings, state/traceability indexes, commit decision and honest blocker report.
roles_and_gates.implementers: Parent may implement all tasks sequentially. Optional I1 split uses parent and one file-disjoint implementer after I1.T1; the gate treats both as implementers.
roles_and_gates.verifier: For EACH increment, a newly launched fresh-context verifier distinct from all that increment's implementers; reads/executes and may add missing tests, but cannot change production source. Replays due checks on integrated tree and independently asserts public outcomes.
roles_and_gates.reviewer: For EACH increment, a second fresh-context read-only reviewer distinct from implementers and verifier. Receives current design, tasks, diff, actual metrics and raw evidence; reconciles due ACs from tree. Prefer different model when available, not a claimed capability.
roles_and_gates.ordering: Implementation and targeted checks -> integrated due checks/actual probe -> fresh independent verification -> fresh independent review -> parent findings dispositions -> commit decision -> dependent increment. Both independent steps are mandatory before EACH commit/next increment, not final-only. Any source/test/contract correction after a verdict invalidates affected proof and reruns affected verification/review; no self-review substitution.
roles_and_gates.due_authority: Only the three gate tasks' proof arrays declare due closure checks. Other task proof arrays name their local feedback checks, not duplicate runtime edges. Future checks do not block early actions; no gate may mark them verified. Checks referenced again mean rerun on current integrated snapshot, not reuse an old green label.
roles_and_gates.functional_vs_quality: A task can have functional implementation VERIFIED when real fixtures correctly demonstrate unavailable/fail behavior. Actual increment quality is separately incomplete if required metrics are unavailable. C-PROBE never turns expected incomplete/fail into a quality pass. Required missing proof cannot be waived by an independent review, VERIFIED-WITH-LIMITATIONS, fixture metric, imported old receipt or parent checkbox. Report functional delivery and quality blockers separately.
roles_and_gates.advance_boundary: Gate tasks finish successfully only with all due proof actually accepted. I2.T1 depends on I1.T4 and I3.T1 depends on I2.T4. If actual required metrics cannot be measured, leave the owning gate blocked and later increments pending; do not call an increment green/closed or silently advance. A parent-authorized limited local preservation commit may retain already independently verified/reviewed functional work, but is NOT gate completion or permission to dispatch dependents. This plan authorizes no waiver or redesign to remove the blocker.
roles_and_gates.guard_bootstrap: I1 uses existing artifact-based independent gates and requires no workflow/adoption artifacts. I2 tests use isolated candidate contracts with real fixture proof to test the protocol; they cannot prove this project's missing metrics. Real adoption later requires ordinary source-bound independent DesignReview; it imports no historical execution. Standalone reports are rerun under admission, not relabeled.
roles_and_gates.commit: Use the existing feature branch, never main/master. Parent checks snapshot/commit matches accepted proof and retains Co-authored-by trailer. No commit is executed by this planning task. Guard close checks an already-created matching commit, so precommit verification/review is mandatory; postcommit hashes must still match the proven source. Artifacts generated by proof are exact output exclusions, not a blanket .ai exclusion.
roles_and_gates.blocked_host: If fresh verifier/reviewer cannot be launched later, record a genuine gate blocker; no inline fallback. Do not launch any agents during this planning assignment.
roles_and_gates.publication: Known GitHub 403/Enterprise Managed User blocker. Do not retry publication or propose credential/remote workarounds. Deliver truthful local state and exact normal finishing instructions only if authorized access later changes.

recovery.R-SOURCE: Stop affected work on snapshot, interface or prerequisite mismatch. Preserve raw evidence; identify changed IDs/claims and reverse dependency closure, reopen only affected tasks/checks, preserve unaffected receipt bytes/IDs, repair approved artifacts via parent and recheck readiness. Do not repair historical evidence into a pass.
recovery.R-MEASURE: Lock only the measurement's owned scope; back up bytes before mutation. On timeout/setup/unclassified outcomes emit incomplete current report, never a kill. Verify original byte/membership hash and narrow cleanup. Intervening external edit -> recovery-required, do not overwrite it from backup. Missing analyzer/configuration -> named unavailable metric and prerequisite, not invented command or automatic install.
recovery.R-PROCESS: Capture run/lock token and known process identity. Guard death, age, root PID absence, best-effort kill or direct-exited callback do not prove descendant death. Unknown spawn/tree -> exit 3, RECOVERY_UNVERIFIED, no unlock/replay/second child. Recover only with r2 RecoveryEvidence and independent validation of supported termination/reset observations; no reset API is assumed. Valid recovery records interruption, never success; due checks rerun.
recovery.R-RETRY: On outer/inner 124/125 record exact command/outcome, inspect only owned process identities, perform concrete safe remedy and retry once with bounds. A second hang is a blocker. No global process-name kills; uncertain ownership follows R-PROCESS.
recovery.R-REVIEW: Retain fresh verifier/reviewer return unchanged and dispositions separately. Functional contradictions reopen the implementation owner; design mismatch returns to Gate 2. Rerun affected tests and both independent acceptance roles before committing or advancing.
recovery.R-EXPERIMENT: Leaked cause/oracle/history, shared-filesystem searches reaching withheld material, or insufficient access records -> blindness not-verified. Preserve evidence and scope the claim; never count fixed fixtures/dry-run as live effectiveness. Missing host/termination capability is a blocker, not permission to invent an API.
recovery.R-DOC: Canonical guidance must agree with current interfaces, source and outcome evidence. Broken links, unsupported-version claims or misleading pass text block the owning task. Correct only assigned current consumers; preserve historical planner records.
